concept.description: Types in an api/controller package. Adjust the pattern for your product.
concept.cypher: MATCH (t:Type) WHERE t.fqn =~ '.*\\.(api|controller|web)\\..*' SET t:Api RETURN count(t) AS apiTypes
MATCH (t:Type) WHERE t.fqn =~ '.*\\.service\\..*' SET t:Service RETURN count(t) AS serviceTypes

concept.description: Types in the persistence layer. One name only — `repository`. Three names for this layer (repository / store / persistence) is what made the ArchUnit layer rule match nothing and pass vacuously; CI now fails a module that reintroduces the others.
concept.cypher: MATCH (t:Type) WHERE t.fqn =~ '.*\\.repository\\..*' SET t:Persistence RETURN count(t) AS persistenceTypes

constraint.description: Enforces architecture/constraints/layering.md — a controller must go through a service. Skipping the service layer is where transaction boundaries and authorization checks get lost.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (api:Api)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(p:Persistence) RETURN api.fqn AS controller, p.fqn AS repository

constraint.description: Enforces architecture/constraints/layering.md — package cycles. A cycle means the two packages are one module pretending to be two: neither can be understood, tested or extracted alone.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (p1:Package)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(p2:Package), (p2)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(p1) WHERE p1.fqn < p2.fqn RETURN p1.fqn AS package, p2.fqn AS cyclicWith

constraint.description:
Enforces architecture/constraints/integration.md — one bounded context must not read another's tables. Cross-context access through the database is invisible to every API contract and survives every refactor of the owning service.
The pattern below compares the segment before `.repository.`; set it to your own context roots.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (t:Type)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(p:Persistence) WHERE NOT t:Persistence AND split(t.fqn, '.repository.')[0] <> split(p.fqn, '.repository.')[0] AND t.fqn =~ '.*\\.(service|api)\\..*' RETURN t.fqn AS accessor, p.fqn AS foreignRepository

constraint.description: Types with an unusually large number of outgoing dependencies. Not an error by itself — a finding. A class that depends on thirty others is usually several classes that were never separated, and it is the one that breaks whenever anything changes.
constraint.cypher: MATCH (t:Type)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(other:Type) WITH t, count(DISTINCT other) AS fanOut WHERE fanOut > 30 RETURN t.fqn AS type, fanOut ORDER BY fanOut DESC
